messages:
maria: Heads-up — bringing up montecarlo14b (14B) quant-int4 canary on a small fleet. Quick summary: accuracy delta minimal on eval set, but latency up and mem fragmentation spike on longer contexts.
ryan: can you paste the perf numbers and config?
maria: perf snippet: ```batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=128, seq_len=1024
int4 w/ per-channel scaling
throughput: 320 tok/s (baseline int8 was 380 tok/s)
p90 latency: 210ms -> 250ms
GPU mem high-water: 24.8GB -> 27.1GB
observed GC-like pauses at ~10s into sustained load```
jeff: ugh that HWM increase looks like fragmentation. Which allocator? cudnn? or we see slab fragmentation in our allocator logs.
maria: allocator: custom-slab-v2 (server image r2026.03). Logs show repeated small alloc/free churn from KV cache prefetch for longer contexts.
dana: did you try microbatching or lowering batch_size? microbatching=4 was mentioned in notes for similar models.
maria: yes, microbatching to 4 drops p90 to 230ms but throughput drops to 260 tok/s. Still some mem spikes.
perf-bot: Benchmark alert — montecarlo14b/int4 canary vs baseline: latency +19%, throughput -15%, mem HWM +9%.
ryan: any quality regressions on the eval set? we need to ensure quant isn't causing decode issues.
maria: ran eval-suite v2 (1000 prompts): chr F1 delta = -0.6%, pass@1 delta = -0.2% — within tolerance but a handful of prompt types (long-dialog) show more divergence.
jeff: hypothesis: int4 kernel code path + batching schedule causes extra KV copies leading to fragmentation and latency. Could also be cache prefetch ordering.
ops-liz: from infra — we saw a few OOMs on canary nodes after sustained load at batch=8+max_new=256. Crash traces attached: `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` inside allocator::allocLarge().
dana: steps: 1) lower default max_new_tokens to 128 for int4 variant on canary 2) enable slot compaction heuristic for slab allocator 3) run targeted long-dialog regression.
ryan: +1. Also add a fallback route: if mem HWM > 26GB return model-variant=int8 or reduce batch automatically.
maria: implemented changes on canary: `defaults: { batch_size: 6, max_new_tokens: 128, microbatch: 2 }` and enabled `slab.compact_period=30s` on allocator. Re-running smoke now.
perf-bot: Smoke results: throughput 295 tok/s, p90 225ms, mem HWM 25.3GB, no OOM for 20m sustained.
maria: quality re-run in progress; early looks stable. Next: longer A/B against int8 on production-like traffic distribution, and we'll run a targeted eval for long-dialog prompt set.
jeff: if fragmentation persists we should pursue a kernel change to avoid extra temp buffers on int4 matmul (cc @ryan for kernel budget).
dana: noted. Add rollout guard to keep default as int8 for customer tier >= dedicated until we have full stability.
ryan: thanks — file a short postmortem if we hit any regression. Otherwise we can ramp canary to 10% after A/B.
maria: will update the onboarding doc with the tunables and add a short benchmark table comparing int4/int8 across batch sizes and max_new_tokens. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
